messages:
maya: Heads-up: regression on runtime when serving qwen-32k v1.2 — FlashAttention probes are choosing SDPA fallback for layers where head_dim=67, causing ~2x per-token latency. Perf profile uploaded.

perf-bot: profile uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/2145678901/qwen32k-v1.2.json

dinesh: Can you paste the relevant stack? Is it hitting Triton fallback or our slow CUDA kernel?

maya: Stack shows kernel_selector -> sdpa_compat_check -> fallback_fastpath. It appears the mask/padding calculation treats head_dim%16 != 0 as unsafe for flash, so we skip the fast vectorized kernel. Repro:
```
./run_infer --model qwen-32k --batch 4 --seq 2048 --heads 67
```
Baseline v1.1 used SDPA-only (no flash probe) and was ~80ms. v1.2 changed probe order to flash-first and now we're at ~180ms.

kevin: 67 is an odd-head case. FlashAttention historically requires 8/16-aligned head widths for vector ops. Did we recently relax alignment checks? Could be the SDPA->flash probe ordering change burned us.

maya: Exactly. Quick canary: set env REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER=sdpa,flash on canary hosts — perf returns to baseline. I'm going to change kernel_selector to treat head_dim%8!=0 as flash-incompatible (so we avoid probing flash for those) and add a masking shim for future work.

dinesh: Sounds good. Short-term mitigation is env toggle and canary rollout. Long-term: add a padded-kv path that avoids extra copying when we add 8-padding. Also add a regression test for qwen-32k in the perf harness.

kevin: I'll review the patch. Add unit test for mask padding and a perf regression alert to Optimize dashboard for qwen-32k (regression >30%): create ticket.

maya: created ticket INF-4127 and linked canary logs: https://redwood.internal/logs/INF-4127/canary

oncall: acknowledged, monitoring latency and errors. ping me if we need rollback. :thumbsup:
